answers.answer: A player rules a clearing if they have more total warriors plus buildings there than each other player. Tokens and pawns do not count. Ordinary ties mean nobody rules; the Eyrie wins a tie for most if it has at least one Eyrie piece there. The Vagabond cannot rule or prevent another player from ruling.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: rule is based on warriors plus buildings; tokens and pawns excluded; ordinary ties, Eyrie tie exception, and Vagabond exception stated.

answers.answer: A normal move takes a positive number of the player's warriors or pawns along a path to an adjacent clearing, and the player must rule the origin or destination or both. Rule is rechecked for each move. The same pieces may move repeatedly, including on multiple moves in one action. Rivers are not paths unless an effect explicitly says they are.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Move (4.2).

answers.answer: The defender may play one matching ambush (birds are wild); the attacker may foil it with a matching ambush. A foiled ambush deals no hits. Otherwise it deals two immediate hits, not capped by defending warriors, and the defender discards it; if no attacking warriors or pawns remain, battle ends. Resolve before-roll effects, roll (higher die is attacker hits and lower is defender hits; ties give equal results), then after-roll effects. Rolled hits are capped by each side's warriors in battle; the Alliance reverses the dice and the Vagabond uses undamaged swords instead of warriors. Add extra hits without a warrior cap and subtract ignored hits. A defender with no warriors makes the attacker deal one extra defenseless hit; the Vagabond is defenseless only if it has no undamaged swords. Each side taking hits chooses its removal order, but must remove all its warriors before its buildings or tokens; both sides deal their counted hits. Removing an enemy building or token scores one VP for the remover, whether attacking or defending and whether or not removal occurred in battle.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Battle (4.3), six steps.

answers.answer: Crafting uses crafting icons at the bottom left of the card, not its suit. Each crafting piece activates once per turn, except the Vagabond can reactivate its pawn by exhausting more hammers. An item card cannot be crafted if that item is absent from the map supply. A persistent effect cannot be crafted if an identical persistent effect is already in the player's play area.
answers.evidence: Actions → Shared movement, crafting and battle: Craft (4.1).

answers.answer: During their own Daylight, a player with at least 10 VP may activate a dominance card from hand, remove their score marker, and stop scoring VP. At the start of their own Birdsong, mouse, rabbit, or fox dominance wins if they rule three clearings of that suit; bird dominance wins if they rule two diagonally opposite corner clearings. The activated card cannot be removed or replaced.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3).

answers.answer: A dominance card that would enter the discard pile is instead placed near the map as available. During their own Daylight, a player may spend a matching card to take an available dominance card into hand. Available bird dominance remains bird, so it must be paid for with a bird card; a bird hand card can pay for a non-bird dominance card.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Dominance (3.3): availability and taking dominance cards.

answers.answer: In a two-player game, remove all four dominance cards before shuffling the shared deck; each player draws three cards. Cover the four R building slots with ruins. The map item supply is 2 boots, 2 bags, 1 crossbow, 1 hammer, 2 swords, 2 tea, and 2 coins; keep the four R-marked ruin items separate, and only Vagabond setup hides those four items under the ruins. Factions set up in letter order: Marquise, Eyrie, Alliance, Vagabond. Setup order is distinct from turn order.
answers.evidence: Setup: standard setup steps 3–7 and faction setup subsections.

answers.answer: Only the Marquise may place pieces in the Keep's clearing, though other players may move pieces into it. The Keep cannot be placed again if removed. Whenever any number of Marquise warriors are removed from a clearing, the Marquise may spend one card matching that clearing to place those warriors in the Keep clearing instead of returning them to supply; this can happen outside battle. Field Hospitals have no destination if the Keep is gone.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Keep and Field Hospitals.

answers.answer: Marquise Daylight starts by crafting with workshops, then allows up to three actions plus one action for each bird card spent outside an action, in any order and number subject to Recruit's limit. March is one compound action of up to two moves; it cannot be interrupted to spend a bird card or take another action. Recruit places one warrior at each recruiter and can be taken only once per turn. Overwork spends a card matching a sawmill's clearing to place one wood there.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Daylight actions: Battle, March, Recruit, Build, Overwork.

answers.answer: To build, choose a clearing the Marquise rules with an open building slot, choose a building type, and take that type's leftmost building from its track. Pay the cost atop its column using wood in the target clearing or in other ruled clearings connected to it through an unbroken chain of ruled clearings. Place the building and score the VP on the newly uncovered track space. The build is illegal if the full wood cost, building, or legal slot is unavailable.
answers.evidence: Marquise de Cat → Daylight: Build.

answers.answer: Eyrie Birdsong proceeds in order: Emergency Orders (draw one if the hand is empty); Add to Decree (add one or two hand cards, with at most one bird card, to any columns); A New Roost. If there are no roosts on the map, place one roost and three warriors in a clearing with the fewest warriors where all those pieces can be placed.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Birdsong, steps 1–3.

answers.answer: The Eyrie crafts with roosts first, then resolves every Decree card column by column in Recruit, Move, Battle, Build order. Within each column it chooses the card order freely; birds are wild. Recruit places a warrior (two with Charismatic) at a roost in a clearing matching the card's suit. Move requires moving at least one warrior from a matching clearing, subject to ordinary movement rules. Battle requires initiating a battle in a matching clearing with Eyrie warriors and an enemy. Build requires placing a roost in a matching clearing the Eyrie rules, with an open slot and no roost already there. If any required action cannot be fully completed, the Eyrie immediately enters Turmoil and cannot skip that card or continue other columns.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Daylight — resolve the Decree.

answers.answer: In Turmoil, lose one VP per bird Decree card, including both Loyal Viziers; discard every Decree card except the Viziers; flip the current leader face down and choose a face-up replacement, flipping all leaders face up first if none are available; then retuck the Viziers in the new leader's columns. Daylight ends and the Eyrie proceeds to Evening, where it still scores from the rightmost empty roost-track space, draws, and discards to five. Turmoil does not remove map warriors or buildings.
answers.evidence: Eyrie Dynasties → Turmoil, in order; Evening, even after turmoil.

answers.answer: Outrage triggers when another player removes sympathy or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing. That player adds one hand card matching the clearing to Supporters, with birds counting; a group move costs one card per affected move, not per warrior. If the player has no matching card, including birds, they show their hand to the Alliance, which draws one card from the deck into Supporters. Supporter capacity still applies: with no base, the stack is capped at five and incoming cards beyond capacity are discarded; with any base, it is unlimited. Merely battling in a sympathetic clearing does not trigger Outrage unless sympathy is removed, and moving only the Vagabond pawn does not trigger it.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Supporters and Outrage.

answers.answer: In Birdsong, the Alliance may Revolt any number of times first, then Spread Sympathy any number of times. Revolt chooses a sympathetic clearing without a base matching a base still on the Alliance board, spends two matching supporters, removes all enemy pieces there, places the matching base, places warriors equal to the number of sympathetic clearings matching that base's printed suit, and places one warrior in the Officers box. Spread Sympathy chooses an unsympathetic clearing adjacent by path to sympathy, or any clearing if no sympathy is on the map; it spends the matching supporters shown above the next sympathy token, plus one matching supporter for Martial Law if one other player has at least three warriors there, then places sympathy and scores the uncovered VP. Revolt and Spread Sympathy are different actions with these separate eligibility and cost rules.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Birdsong: Revolt and Spread Sympathy.

answers.answer: To Train, the Alliance spends a hand card matching a clearing with a base and places one supply warrior in the Officers box; Supporters cannot pay this cost. In Evening, it may take military operations up to its number of officers; Organize removes one Alliance warrior from an unsympathetic clearing, places sympathy there, and scores the uncovered VP, with no supporter, adjacency, or Martial Law cost, but legal token placement is still required. When a base is removed, discard supporters matching its clearing, including birds, remove half the officers rounded up, and, if no bases remain, discard excess supporters down to five.
answers.evidence: Woodland Alliance → Losing a base; Daylight Train; Evening Organize.

answers.answer: At Birdsong, refresh two exhausted items per tea already face up on the Refresh track, then three more; tea refreshed during this step gives no bonus refresh in that step. The Vagabond may then Slip to an adjacent clearing or forest without exhausting boots, including into hostile warriors, ignoring effects that prevent movement out of a clearing. A normal Daylight Move exhausts one boot plus one extra boot if the destination has any warriors of any Hostile faction; it ignores rule, cannot enter a forest, and from a forest can move only to an adjacent clearing. If the Vagabond is in a forest in Evening, Rest returns damaged items to the Satchel and flips them face up, with ready tea/coins/bags moving to tracks if possible; Rest does not refresh undamaged exhausted items. It always draws one card plus one per face-up coin on track, even after Rest.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Birdsong Refresh and Slip; Daylight Move; Evening Rest and draw.

answers.answer: Explore exhausts a torch in a ruin's clearing; take one hidden item face up into Satchel or a track, scoring one VP if an item is taken. Remove the ruin when its last item is taken, freeing the slot. For a Quest, choose a face-up quest matching the clearing and exhaust its two listed items; complete it and choose either VP equal to the number of matching completed quests including this one, or draw two cards. Reveal a replacement quest. Repair exhausts a hammer to move one damaged item to Satchel without changing its current face; ready tea, coins, or bags move to tracks if space is available.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Daylight: Explore, Quest, Repair.

answers.answer: Removing one warrior of a non-Hostile faction immediately makes that faction Hostile to the Vagabond. During battle on the Vagabond's own turn, Infamy scores one extra VP per hostile piece removed, except the warrior that first made the faction Hostile; ordinary points for buildings/tokens still apply. Infamy is not scored while defending on another player's turn or from Strike. Aid cannot move a faction out of Hostile, though it can still obtain a crafted item. Strike exhausts a crossbow to remove one enemy warrior in the clearing; only if that enemy has no warriors there may it remove another piece of that faction. Strike is not battle and gives no Infamy.
answers.evidence: Vagabond → Relationships: Hostile and Infamy; Daylight Strike; Aid note.

answers.answer: The Vagabond cannot activate normal dominance to win. With four or more players, during its own Daylight at 10 or more VP, it may activate a dominance card to form a coalition with a player not already in a coalition who has the lowest VP among players other than the Vagabond; it chooses among ties. It places its score marker on that player's faction board and stops scoring. If the partner wins, the Vagabond also wins, including when the partner wins by dominance. Coalition partners are not enemies, and a Hostile partner becomes Indifferent; coalition alone does not grant Allied relationship powers.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions → Vagabond coalition (9.2.8).
